In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increasing energy supply per capita is a major determinant for increasing BMI in high-income countries.
the increase in energy supply is associated with the increase in mean BMI, but that this association does not necessarily imply a cause-and-effect relationship between the two.
the increasing energy supply is associated with increasing BMI in most of the countries studied, while the effect of energy supply from fat and sweeteners was less pronounced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increasing trend in energy supply in the past decades is the main reason for the increase in obesity and overweight in most countries.
the increase of energy supply per capita is a major factor in the increase of obesity in western countries.
the increasing trends in BMI in most countries are closely associated with increasing trends in energy supply per capita.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the obesity epidemic in Western European countries and China can be partly attributed to the increase of energy supply.
the obesity epidemic is not a natural phenomenon, but is caused by the increase in food availability and energy intake.
the obesity epidemic is not a result of genetic or cultural changes but rather a result of changes in energy intake and expenditure.
